en: Contrary to old textbooks, the Philippines officially has 7,641 islands, not the previously taught number of 7,107.
The Cagayan River, not the Pasig River, is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers.
Lake Mainit, not Laguna de Bay, is the deepest lake in the Philippines, reaching a maximum depth of 122 meters.
Although often called the smallest, Taal Volcano's main crater lake actually contains Vulcan Point, the true smallest active volcano.
Mayon Volcano has its perfect cone shape precisely because of frequent lava eruptions, not because it is dormant and unchanging.
Palawan is administratively part of the Mimaropa region in Luzon, not the Visayas island group as many mistakenly believe.
The Banaue Rice Terraces are not a UNESCO World Heritage site, as only five specific Cordillera clusters hold that official title.
The West Philippine Sea refers only to the eastern parts of the South China Sea within Philippine jurisdiction, not the entire sea.
The Philippines has four distinct climate types based on rainfall, rather than just the simple wet and dry seasons people assume.
The Philippine eagle is the world's largest eagle by length and wing area, not by overall body weight as often assumed.
The Philippine tarsier is not the world's smallest primate, as that specific title actually belongs to the pygmy mouse lemur of Madagascar.
Mount Apo is the highest Philippine mountain at 2,954 meters, not Mount Pulag, which is a common misconception among hikers.
